headline: Sandon Capital notes Tabcorp's decision to seek ACT authorisation for the Tatts merger, effectively conceding a lessening of competition but pursuing a net benefit argument
reasoning: TAH chose to bypass the ACCC review and go directly to the Australian Competition Tribunal for an 'authorisation to proceed', which allows the ACT to weigh merger benefits against competitive harm rather than the ACCC's narrower competition-only lens. Sandon Capital interprets this as TAH conceding there will be a lessening of competition but hoping to make a net benefit case. The rise in TAH's share price during the month suggests the market ascribes some likelihood to the merger proceeding.
quote: The more notable occurrences during the month were TAH's decision to circumvent the Australian Consumer and Competition Commission (ACCC) review of the merger proposal by submitting an application directly to the Australian Competition Tribunal (ACT) for an "authorisation to proceed". The ACT is able to weigh the benefits of the merger against any reduction in competition, whereas the ACCC has a narrower remit of considering whether a proposed transaction will lessen competition. By going directly to the ACT, we believe TAH is conceding that there will be a lessening of competition, but hopes it can make the case for an overall net benefit argument.
